extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners reviewing eligibility guidance)
extracted.subtask_description: A reference chart for examiners that summarizes court decisions bearing on patent subject-matter eligibility, listing citation, patent/application numbers, subject matter, eligibility outcome, classifications, and cross-references to the 2014 Interim Eligibility Guidance and examples. Designed to help identify applications that may require detailed eligibility analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal citation and opinion link
rubrics_metrics.description: a legal citation and, if available, a link to the entire court opinion (if no link is available, a parallel citation to the U.S.P.Q reporter is also provided)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full case citation and, where possible, an internet link to the opinion so examiners can read the court's reasoning; if the opinion link is not available include the U.S.P.Q. parallel citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent or application number(s) at issue
rubrics_metrics.description: the U.S. patent number(s) or application number(s) at issue
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List all relevant patent or application numbers so examiners can locate file histories and claim sets; include multiple numbers when several related patents/applications are implicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter summary
rubrics_metrics.description: the subject matter of the patent/application
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise description of the claimed invention's field and high-level features (e.g., 'Formulation and trading of risk management – Methods, systems, computer readable media') to enable quick topical comparison with pending applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility conclusion (eligible/ineligible)
rubrics_metrics.description: whether the claims were eligible or ineligible (note that a finding applies to all claims in the patent/application unless otherwise noted)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate the court's ultimate determination for the claims (eligible or ineligible). If the court specified claim-level outcomes, identify which specific claims were held eligible/ineligible (e.g., 'claims 1, 5-6 ineligible; claims 2 & 7 eligible').

rubrics_metrics.name: USPC and CPC classification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the patent classification codes (USPC and CPC) assigned to the patent/application to help examiners find similarly classified cases, but do not treat classification similarity as dispositive of eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference to 2014 IEG and eligibility examples
rubrics_metrics.description: a notation of where the case is discussed (if applicable) in the 2014 Interim Guidance on Subject Matter Eligibility and/or the eligibility examples (index provided in Appendix 2)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate Section/Example numbers in the 2014 IEG where the case is cited or analyzed to assist examiners in applying the IEG framework and example reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-level claim detail notes
rubrics_metrics.description: notation when the court’s eligibility determination applies to some claims but not others (e.g., '’479: asserted claims 33-34. ’510, ’720, and ’375: all claims.')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a court's decision identifies claim-specific outcomes, record those specifics (claim numbers and which claims were affected) so examiners can compare specific claim language rather than relying on blanket statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat about framework differences
rubrics_metrics.description: the courts’ analyses in these decisions do not necessarily employ the Alice eligibility framework, which is explained in the 2014 IEG, because most of the cases were decided prior to the 2014 IEG
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should not assume court reasoning maps exactly onto the Alice/IEG framework; read the court's reasoning and apply the IEG consistently while recognizing differences in analytical approach across decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-specificity reminder
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to remember that each case turns on its own facts. Therefore, the mere fact that a pending application may be similarly classified to a patent or an application in this chart, or have similar subject matter, does not necessarily indicate an eligibility issue. Identification of a judicial exception in a claim merely indicates further analysis for eligibility should be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the chart as a starting point for further analysis rather than as a dispositive determination; similarity in classification or subject matter signals that an examiner should perform a detailed eligibility analysis on the particular claim language and facts of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table fields / organization for each case
rubrics_metrics.description: For each case (arranged by court and in reverse chronological order), the tables provide the following information: (1) citation/link, (2) patent/app numbers, (3) subject matter, (4) eligible/ineligible determination, (5) USPC/CPC classification, and (6) notation of where discussed in 2014 IEG/examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified table format and ordering (by court, reverse chronological) so examiners can consistently scan and compare entries; update the chart as future decisions become available and annotate where cases were used in IEG examples or training.
